extracted.intended_audience: startup founders and small businesses seeking NSF SBIR/STTR seed funding (tech entrepreneurs, including first-time founders and companies from all U.S. states and territories)
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance and program-level criteria for startups applying to the NSF SBIR/STTR seed funding program; focuses on eligibility, program terms, target technologies, stage of development, and the key review considerations (innovativeness, commercial potential, societal impact).

rubrics_metrics.name: Funding amount and terms
rubrics_metrics.description: We invest up to $2 million in seed funding. And take zero equity.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Seed capital for early stage product development. We offer funding for early stage R&D and take no equity in your company — you retain full control over your team, the direction of your work, and your intellectual property.

rubrics_metrics.name: Eligible applicants / invitation to all tech entrepreneurs
rubrics_metrics.description: We invite all tech entrepreneurs. Our program fosters and encourages participation in innovation and entrepreneurship from all Americans as well as first-time entrepreneurs from all 50 states and U.S. territories.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Implied target applicant is startups/small businesses and first-time founders across the U.S.; the program emphasizes nationwide and inclusive participation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Target technologies — deep technologies
rubrics_metrics.description: We support research and development of deep technologies - those that are based on discoveries in fundamental science and engineering.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Deep tech is defined here as technology based on fundamental science/engineering discoveries; applicants should be developing technologies with a strong scientific/engineering foundation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Scope of technology and markets funded
rubrics_metrics.description: We fund startups across nearly all technology areas and markets like artificial intelligence, energy, medical devices, robotics, semiconductors, and many more.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The program is broad in technical scope; applicants in a wide range of technology domains (examples listed) are eligible. Applicants should consult 'View what we fund' for further detail and examples.

rubrics_metrics.name: Stage focus — early-stage R&D / product development
rubrics_metrics.description: Seed capital for early stage product development. We offer funding for early stage R&D...
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The program targets early-stage research and development and initial product development activities; applicants should be seeking support for early R&D and commercialization preparation rather than late-stage/scale-up financing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Review criterion — Innovativeness
rubrics_metrics.description: As we review applications, we consider your technology’s innovativeness...
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reviewers will evaluate the novelty and technical advancement of the proposed technology. The program's emphasis on 'deep technologies' suggests innovation grounded in fundamental science/engineering breakthroughs will be favorably viewed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Review criterion — Commercial potential
rubrics_metrics.description: As we review applications, we consider your ... commercial potential...
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicants must demonstrate pathways to commercialization, market opportunity, and potential for commercial success (the program explicitly funds startups 'to build deep technologies for commercial success'). Success stories (customers, acquisitions, deployments) are presented as examples of desired outcomes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Review criterion — Possible societal impact
rubrics_metrics.description: As we review applications, we consider your ... possible societal impact.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Proposals should articulate potential societal benefits or impacts (e.g., safety improvements, environmental remediation, healthcare advances). The site highlights examples (life‑saving robot, environmental cleanup technologies, medical devices) to illustrate impactful outcomes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Program support resources for applicants
rubrics_metrics.description: We can help fund your technology. Attend a webinar. Join our regular webinars to learn more.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: NSF provides informational resources (webinars, events) to help prospective applicants understand the program and application process; applicants are encouraged to use these resources.

rubrics_metrics.name: Program objective — commercialization emphasis
rubrics_metrics.description: We fund startups to build deep technologies for commercial success.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Beyond technical merit, the program's goal is to move deep-tech discoveries toward commercial products; proposals should address commercialization strategy and business development as part of the application narrative.
